related_questions.question: What are the new rules for tourists in Spain?

text_blocks.snippet: Spain has introduced new tourist regulations, primarily focusing on managing overtourism and enhancing security, rather than outright banning tourists. These changes include increased tourist taxes, stricter short-term rental regulations, tougher public drinking laws, and limits on tourist access to certain beaches and natural areas. Additionally, new rules require more extensive personal information from tourists and hosts.

list.title: Increased Tourist Taxes:
list.snippet: Popular destinations like Barcelona, Palma de Mallorca, and the Canary Islands are raising tourist tax rates for hotels, cruises, and short-term rentals.

list.title: Stricter Short-Term Rental Regulations:
list.snippet: Cities like Madrid, Seville, and Valencia are implementing tighter rules on short-term rentals, potentially limiting availability and increasing costs.

list.title: Tougher Public Drinking Laws:
list.snippet: Restrictions on alcohol consumption in public spaces have been expanded in nightlife hotspots, with fines for violations.

list.title: Limits on Tourist Access:
list.snippet: Some beaches and natural areas are implementing daily visitor caps to address overcrowding and environmental concerns.

list.title: Increased Personal Information Requirements:
list.snippet: Hotels and travel agencies are now required to collect and store more personal data from tourists, including potentially sensitive information like bank details.

list.title: Travel Insurance Requirement:
list.snippet: Non-EU visitors are now required to show proof of travel insurance at the border.

list.title: Proof of Sufficient Funds:
list.snippet: Tourists may need to demonstrate they have enough money to cover their stay, in addition to showing proof of accommodation.

list.title: Return Ticket Requirement:
list.snippet: Tourists may be asked to show proof of a return or onward travel ticket.

list.title: Banned Beach Items and Behavior:
list.snippet: Certain items and actions are banned on some beaches, including smoking, playing music, cooking, and public sex.

list.title: Resident-Only Zones:
list.snippet: Some areas, like the town center of Sóller in Mallorca, have restricted access for hire cars, creating resident-only zones.

list.title: Walking Tour Caps:
list.snippet: In Palma, Mallorca, walking tours are limited to 20 people per group.
